newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX volatilities tread water, await FOMC.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX volatilities tread water, await FOMC.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options treaded water in quiet U.S. morning business as the market awaited Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, dealers said.
Despite a largely range-bound spot, volatilities remained underpinned -- so far -- by concerns over a Federal Reserve credit tightening at the meeting.

"Normally, you'd expect a sell-on-the-fact type of reaction after an event like this," said Kyoko Hiramatsu, a senior dealer at Bank of Yokohama in New York. "But you can't be sure because of the unstable U.S. asset markets."

"With Easter and the fiscal year-end for Japanese companies (at end-March) coming up, short-dated volatilities are liable to come under pressure after FOMC, but no one wants to be short gamma before an event like that," she added.
A short-gamma position, typically a result of selling shorter-dated options, benefits from time decay but is vulnerable to big swings in spot.

Short-dated dollar/mark could be particularly vulnerable, given the very flat volatility curve, traders said. One-month to one-year dollar/mark implied volatilities were virtually flat at 9.8/10.1 percent, barely changed from Friday.
One-month and one-year dollar/yen were also unchanged from Friday at 10.5/10.8 and 11.1/11.3 percent respectively.
Volatilities for standard one-week options dipped despite the FOMC event risk because of the upcoming Easter weekend.
"It's simply because there's a holiday in there," a trader at a French bank in New York said, adding that options expiring this week were still relatively well-bid because of the FOMC meeting.
Most U.S. and European financial markets will be shut on Friday and many U.S. traders are likely to go home early on Thursday. Monday is also a holiday in many European countries.

Risk perception was somewhat skewed toward the dollar's upside, although traders said the market remained sensitive to the dollar's approach toward either side of its recent 120-125 yen and 1.66-1.72 mark ranges.
Risk reversals, the pricing differential between puts and calls, were marginally favoring mark puts in dollar/mark and yen puts in dollar/yen.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal stood at 0.0/0.3 percent in favor of mark puts in dollar/mark and 0.1/0.3 percent for yen puts in dollar/yen.
